summary: Some allowances in your salary are partly or wholly free of tax. An allowance for expenses of the job, such as a uniform or conveyance for duties, is exempt only as far as you actually spent the money on that purpose. An allowance for your children's education or hostel is exempt up to a fixed amount a month for each child, for at most two children. An employee who is blind, deaf and dumb, or orthopaedically handicapped may have a transport allowance for commuting exempt up to a fixed amount a month. In the default regime only a few of these survive, such as conveyance for duties and that transport allowance.

routes.name: Allowances for expenses of the job
routes.description: Uniform and conveyance for duties: exempt up to what you actually spent, and no more than the allowance paid.

routes.name: Allowances for your children
routes.description: Children education and hostel allowances: exempt up to a fixed amount a month for each child, for at most two children.

routes.name: Transport allowance for a disabled employee
routes.description: Commuting allowance for an employee who is blind, deaf and dumb, or orthopaedically handicapped: exempt up to a fixed amount for each month it was paid, and no more than the allowance paid. Which disabilities qualify, and whether the amount depends on the city, differ by year.

routes.name: Other allowances
routes.description: Travel on tour or transfer, daily allowance, helper, academic pursuits, and allowances for the armed forces or remote areas.

conditions.reason: Not built: rarely on a salary slip, or outside this product's scope.

disqualifiers.description: In the default regime only the allowances the rules list survive; uniform and the children's allowances do not.
